summary: No test appears to drive render.ProvenanceRegion's refusal through Render or PostBodies, so dropping this error check would silently omit the disclosure rather than stop the draft, unnoticed.
evidence: render.ProvenanceRegion returns an error on one input: a region whose content carries render.Reserved, which in practice is a rule rationale holding "<!-- cr:" (internal/render/provenance.go:73). internal/render/provenance_test.go:70 covers that refusal inside render, but nothing exercises how draft.go:120-123 reacts to it. The only Rationales map any test builds is internal/draft/provenance_test.go:18, whose rationale is benign, and a repository-wide search for a rationale carrying the reserved sequence finds the string only in render's own expected output. If this check were removed and the error ignored, provenance would be empty and the block would render with no provenance region at all, which is the disclosure that section exists to force. Rule rationales are project-owned text, so the input is reachable rather than hypothetical. Asked rather than asserted, because I did not run it; proposal x31902 is the mutation that would settle it.
